channel.title: Solar & Geomagnetic Alerts
channel.description: Significant solar flares, solar eruptions, geomagnetic storms, radiation storms, solar wind shocks and power-grid risk. WATCH = worth keeping an eye on; WARNING = a significant event is likely or under way; ALERT = an extreme event. Times are UTC.

item.title: WATCH: Potentially dangerous sunspot AR4581 faces Earth, S08E53 (complex magnetic layout, beta-gamma-delta)
item.description: Level: WATCH. Sunspot region AR4581 (AR means active region; this is NOAA's number for it) is facing Earth, at S08E53 on the Sun, and has: a complex magnetic layout, class BGD (beta-gamma-delta), the kind most likely to produce major flares. Shape class Dai; covers 70 millionths of the Sun's visible half; 17 spots. Based on NOAA's region summary for 2026-11-18 UTC (updated daily, so up to a day old). Sunspot regions are where solar flares and eruptions come from; because this one faces Earth, anything it throws out could be aimed our way.
